::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [1861]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown. This fragment printed by Christabel Maxwell, <i>[Mrs Gatty and Mrs Ewing](other_books/otherbook_306.qmd)</i>, (1949) 140-1.
:::

I quite agree with [you](people/person_549.qmd) as to the promise of power in [Aunt Judy](people/person_494.qmd)’s doings . . . tell her that I shall like to have her intended story.[^1] I like to hear that you are about one of the Aunt Judy race too, but really between Aunt Judy herself and you *as* Aunt Judy, it is not easy to distinguish in one’s letters which one means, though there is no such difficulty in the *[Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd)*. She shows herself entirely original by so completely avoiding your style.

---

[^1]: Gatty’s daughter, Juliana Horatia Gatty (1841-1885), later Ewing, was the model for the persona Gatty adopted for her “Aunt Judy” tales in the *MP* in 1858. In 1861 Juliana began sending her own fictional tales to the *MP*. These tales were collected and published as *Melchior’s Dream and Other Stories* (1862) and *The Brownies* (1865). After the founding of *Aunt Judy’s Magazine* (edited by Gatty) in 1866 Ewing’s works were first published there.
